Create an isolated ruined medieval fortress on a rocky rise beside a broad shallow muddy river, enclosed by rolling terrain and pale eroded mountains. Place one compact castle at one end, combining a rectangular keep, round and square towers, broken curtain walls, roofless chambers, and scattered red banners. Extend a long straight fortified stone bridge across the water, supported by repeated arches and ending at a small roofed gateway. Near the castle, add damaged wooden ramps, stairs, platforms, and irregular piles rising from the water. Scatter shoreline boulders, low vegetation, and a few dark tree clusters. Keep the fortress and bridge as the only major built elements, with generous open space and warm low sunlight.

Create an isolated ruined medieval fortress on a rocky rise beside a broad shallow muddy river, enclosed by rolling terrain and pale eroded mountains. Place one compact castle at one end, combining a rectangular keep, round and square towers, broken curtain walls, roofless chambers, and scattered red banners. Extend a long straight fortified stone bridge across the water, supported by repeated arches and ending at a small roofed gateway. Near the castle, add damaged wooden ramps, stairs, platforms, and irregular piles rising from the water. Scatter shoreline boulders, low vegetation, and a few dark tree clusters. Keep the fortress and bridge as the only major built elements, with generous open space and warm low sunlight.

    === GROUND ===
    Build the FLOOR FIRST, before placing anything else. Call the benchmark
    tool `ground_pass` as your first build action: it carpets the whole 200 m
    plate deterministically from a tile chosen for this scene. If you skip it,
    and do not tile a floor yourself, the scene renders as objects floating
    over empty space -- which is a failed reconstruction no matter how good
    the massing is. These palette entries are also flat surfaces you can tile
    by hand if you prefer:
